_comment: Which touch panel drives which display.
Both panels report the same libinput name/vendor/product and carry no
serial number, so they can only be told apart by USB topology.
Matching a PANEL (ranked, first hit wins; a tie within a rank is refused):
usb_path      - udev ID_PATH, exact. The primary key.
usb_port      - substring of ID_PATH, then of the resolved /sys path.
usb_revision  - udev ID_USB_REVISION (USB bcdDevice). Port-independent
fallback, used only when unique across panels, so a
panel keeps working if replugged into a different port.
ON THIS BOX usb_path/usb_port are deliberately EMPTY, and matching runs on
usb_revision alone. The panels do not keep a stable USB port across boots:
the bottom-right panel came up on 12.1 at one boot and 13.1 at the next,
because the monitors' built-in hubs re-enumerate in whatever order they
wake. Since usb_path is rank 0 it BEATS usb_revision, so a pinned port that
the other panel later lands on would confidently map the wrong screen --
worse than not matching at all. bcdDevice is a firmware property, not a
topology one: 0600 (left) and 0200 (right) are stable and unique here.
Only re-add usb_path if the panels are ever moved onto a hub that keeps
its port numbering across a power cycle.
Choosing its OUTPUT:
edid_hash     - md5 of the monitor's raw EDID. Preferred: connector
names renumber (this box has DP-1, DP-3, HDMI-A-1,
HDMI-A-4), but the EDID hash does not. Resolved against
/sys/class/drm/*/edid at apply time.
output        - connector name. Used only if edid_hash finds nothing,
and as documentation of the intent.
Discover values:
scripts/touchscreen-mapping-daemon.py --status
udevadm info --query=property --name=/dev/input/event11 | grep ^ID_PATH=
for c in /sys/class/drm/card*-*/; do echo "$c $(md5sum $c/edid)"; done
kscreen-doctor -o
After editing:  systemctl --user reload touchscreen-mapping.service
